solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Foreign dish I served after noisy talk over doughnuts?

indicators.note: the I is dished up after the chatter, so it follows it in the answer
in a down entry the first part sits over the next

parts.note: to yak is to chatter noisily, so yak is noisy talk
tori is the plural of torus, the mathematician's doughnut shape

explanation.surface: A diner is served an exotic dish after loud chat over some doughnuts.
explanation.walkthrough: TORI, the plural of torus, is a ring or doughnut shape, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Yakitori is Japanese skewered grilled chicken, a dish from abroad for a British solver.

clue.text: Extract one trapped in overturned airline

indicators.note: the numeral is caught inside the other piece, so it goes within it
in a down clue the airline's code is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: KLM is the Dutch national airline
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A passenger is pulled out after being stuck on an upturned plane.
explanation.definitionFit: To milk something is to draw out or exploit it, a verb sense of extracting.

clue.text: Pee on ice dancing cozzie

indicators.note: letters that dance about move into a new order

explanation.surface: A cheeky image of someone relieving themselves on an ice rink while dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cozzie' is British and Australian slang for a swimming costume.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-piece is a swimsuit made in a single garment, which is what a cozzie is.

clue.text: Best place to turn over when following article

indicators.note: the turned place comes after the article in the answer

parts.note: the definite article is the word the

indicators.note: the word for place is flipped round, read backwards

parts.note: a spot is a place or location

explanation.surface: A tip about the ideal place to flip something over after reading an article.
explanation.definitionFit: The tops is an informal phrase meaning the very finest, as in 'she's the tops'.

clue.text: Bush fire, unrestrained, destroyed pride

indicators.note: something destroyed is wrecked, so the letters are broken and reassembled
with its restraints, its outer letters, taken off the word fire keeps only its middle

explanation.surface: An uncontrolled bush fire wrecks someone's pride and joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unrestrained' strips fire to IR; 'destroyed' then rearranges BUSH plus IR.
explanation.definitionFit: Hubris is overweening arrogance, the excessive pride that classically comes before a fall.

clue.text: Book opening backed after journalist takes hint

indicators.note: the turned opening comes after the earlier pieces

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist
one who takes a hint gets wind of something, wind being the hint received

indicators.note: backed means turned back, so the word for opening is read in reverse

parts.note: a door is an opening into a room

explanation.surface: A reporter gets a tip-off and reverses through the opening of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mystery of Edwin Drood is Dickens's unfinished last novel, so the title names a book.

clue.text: Lure beginning to reveal one in public

indicators.note: the beginning of the word reveal is only its first letter
the numeral goes inside the word for public

parts.note: something done in the open is public; open means public
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tempting bait starts to show one thing out in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: To rope someone in is to persuade or entice them to take part, much as luring does.

clue.text: Folk swimming for Calais? No thanks

indicators.note: no here means without, so the word for thanks is taken away

parts.note: natation is the French word for swimming, as used in Calais
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: People swimming across to Calais politely refuse help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For Calais' asks for the French word; NATATION is also a rare English word for swimming.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation is a people, the folk of one country.

clue.text: Harry's track, an old song

parts.note: to harry someone is to hound them; the 's is just 'is'
to dog someone is to track or follow them

explanation.surface: Somebody named Harry has a track that turns out to be an oldie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name; it is the verb meaning to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: Hound Dog is the 1950s rock and roll hit famously recorded by Elvis Presley.

clue.text: Lidless dip tips over, causing stain

indicators.note: without its lid, its top letter, the word for dip loses its first letter

parts.note: to sink is to dip or go down

indicators.note: over here means turned over, so the word for tips is read backwards

parts.note: tips are tops, the pointed ends of things

explanation.surface: A pen dipped without its cap tips over and leaves a mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lidless' removes the first letter of SINK; 'over' turns TOPS into SPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkspot is a blot of spilt ink, a kind of stain.

clue.text: Thief's assistant stopping luxury car

indicators.note: the assistant stops up the car, plugging the gap inside it

parts.note: RR is short for Rolls-Royce, the classic luxury car
an aide is an assistant

explanation.surface: A burglar's helper blocks a getaway limousine.
explanation.definitionFit: A raider is someone who makes a robbing attack, a kind of thief or plunderer.

clue.text: I sit naked having nothing to eat

indicators.note: stripped naked, the word sit loses its outer letters

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone sits there in the nude with no food to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker but is the definition: I is the chemical symbol for this element.
explanation.definitionFit: The chemical symbol of the element with atomic number 53 is the letter I.

clue.text: Unfortunately miss urinal in isolation?

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so these letters go astray into a new order

explanation.surface: A sorry tale of missing the urinal, leaving one standing apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Insularism is the narrow outlook of an island people, cut off in isolation from others.

clue.text: Time to abandon Seat Panda lost in US city

indicators.note: lost means gone astray, so these letters are set in a new order
time leaves the word Seat, so its T is dropped

explanation.surface: A driver loses time after their little Seat Panda car gets lost in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To abandon' drops T from SEAT, leaving SEA; 'lost' shuffles SEA plus PANDA. The Seat Panda was a small Spanish car.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasadena is a city in Los Angeles County, California, home of the Rose Bowl.

clue.text: Prefect ultimately sends out those that sponge off snitches?

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter of Prefect

parts.note: to issue is to send out or distribute

explanation.surface: A school prefect finally expels the freeloaders who live off informers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snitch' is British slang for the nose; tissues sponge off noses, not off informers.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper handkerchiefs wipe a runny nose, and snitch is slang for a nose.

clue.text: Nothing's too much around king, say, of an old empire

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing; the 's is just 'is'

indicators.note: turned around, the abbreviation for too much reads backwards

parts.note: OTT stands for over the top, too much
a king is an example of a man, a chess piece

explanation.surface: No excess is too much for a regal figure of a bygone empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' reverses the abbreviation for over the top; 'king, say' is an example of a chess man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ottoman Empire was the Turkish empire that lasted until 1922, so this adjective describes it.

clue.text: Formal bling worn by mum holding a single drink

indicators.note: the combined piece holds the single numeral inside it
the bling worn by mum goes around her, so mum sits inside it

parts.note: a tiara is jewellery worn on formal occasions
ma is an informal word for mum
I is the Roman numeral for one, a single

explanation.surface: Mother in her finest tiara clutches a solitary glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worn by' puts mum inside the bling; 'holding' then takes in the single numeral near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Tia Maria is a coffee liqueur, a brand of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Narrative repeated about bourgeois novels

indicators.note: brought about, the first letter of the doubled word moves round to the end
repeated means the narrative word appears twice in a row

parts.note: a saga is a long narrative story

explanation.surface: A long story told over and over about middle-class books.
explanation.walkthrough: SAGASAGA has its first S moved round to the end by 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aga sagas are British novels of rural middle-class family life, named after the Aga range cooker.

clue.text: Outcast husband blocking devious e-mails

indicators.note: the husband blocks the way by standing inside the jumbled letters
devious means twisting, so the letters wind into a new order

explanation.surface: A spouse gets in the way of some sneaky electronic messages, then is cast out.
explanation.definitionFit: Ishmael, son of Abraham, was driven into the desert, so his name stands for any outcast.

clue.text: Many a Monk clue half-reverses when jumbled

indicators.note: jumbled letters are mixed up into a new order
half of the word reverses, here its second four letters

explanation.surface: The setter Monk confesses a clue of theirs is half back to front once scrambled.
explanation.walkthrough: Monk is this puzzle's setter, so the surface is self-referential; the anagram uses CLUE plus RSES, the back half of 'reverses'.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks typically live withdrawn from the world, and hermits who shun society are recluses.

clue.text: Perhaps fleas oddly adore biting nothing back

indicators.note: back means read the other way, so the whole piece is turned round
the odd letters bite into nothing, holding it in their mouth
oddly picks the letters in odd positions of adore

parts.note: zip is slang for nothing

explanation.surface: Fleas strangely love chewing on nothing in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' gives AOE, which bites round slang for nothing to make AOZIPE; 'back' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Epizoa are parasites living on an animal's surface, and fleas are one example.

clue.text: Notable gesture that's extremely awful

parts.note: a sign is a gesture, such as a wave of the hand

indicators.note: the extremes of awful are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A conspicuous wave of the hand that is truly dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Signal as an adjective means striking or remarkable, as in a signal achievement.

clue.text: Concerning a specific chain of thought one lost when girl's around

indicators.note: the girl goes around the shortened thought, holding it inside

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name; the 's is just 'is'

indicators.note: one is lost, so the numeral drops out of the word for thought

parts.note: an idea is a thought
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone loses their train of thought whenever a certain woman is nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chain of thought' looks like one phrase; the definition ends at 'chain', the mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: Andean means relating to the Andes, the mountain range running down South America.

clue.text: Lass I love rejected a very large plant

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so these pieces read in reverse

parts.note: a lass is a girl
love is zero in tennis, shown as O

explanation.surface: A girl confesses her love was spurned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks botanical; it means industrial installation.
explanation.definitionFit: An offshore drilling platform is a huge industrial installation, plant in the engineering sense.

clue.text: Blimey, country shunning our queen is a pain

parts.note: my! and blimey are both exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: shunning means avoiding, so the queen is removed from the country

parts.note: Algeria is a North African country
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Britain's queen

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a nation snubbing the British monarch is a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Myalgia is the medical term for muscle ache, a kind of bodily pain.

clue.text: Chickpea is good with butter

indicators.note: with joins the two pieces side by side

parts.note: a ram is an animal that butts, so a butter

explanation.surface: A dietary claim that chickpeas go well with butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' is not the spread but one who butts.
explanation.definitionFit: Gram is a name for the chickpea and other pulses grown in India.

clue.text: They suffer taking speed, as part- timers might do?

indicators.note: taking means adding, so the next piece joins on

parts.note: Job is the biblical figure of patient suffering, so Jobs are sufferers
to hare is to run at speed

explanation.surface: Some people suffer from taking amphetamines, as casual workers might.
explanation.definitionFit: Two part-time workers may split one full-time post between them.

clue.text: At home and not at home to some extent

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
to be away is to be not at home

explanation.surface: A contradiction: being both in and out of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: In a way is an idiom meaning partly, in some respects.
